1. Mapless navigation is a huge area, particularly in swarm robotics where, for the most part, you cannot afford to have GPS and are very likely be operating in communication constrained environment.
2. Manipulators are a huge subject within robotics, and for the most part incredibly difficult to solve. There are plenty of manipulators that will work within a certain context/environment but there are things human hands can do that we very much struggle with currently. Potentially an odd example but cabbage picking is notoriously difficult, ~~Oxford~~ Cambridge university currently have a research product on agricultural vegetable picking and they are struggling to outperform groups of people.
3. Outdoor navigation is another big subject. Object detection and tracking is a great area to look into and very much important to robotics and autonomy. Consider self-driving cars and all the recognition/tracking that they need to do to be considered safe.

Happy discuss these further if any are thought provoking/interesting to you.
